answer: Sybil resistance here rests on a per-identity toll. Each new address must solve a proof-of-work puzzle keyed to current chain state, so a clone farm cannot recycle one stale solution; every fresh key re-solves it alone. Blocks credit only the key that mined them, so splitting effort across thousands of addresses forfeits the accrual one honest miner builds on a long-lived terrace. A bonded deposit is slashed when linked keys prove shared control. Marginal cost per identity stays flat while reward per identity falls, so an ocean of sockpuppets costs far more than it earns, with no opal of gain.
